Insert today’s Hijri (Islamic) date, wit: Insert today’s Hijri (Islamic) date, with month names in English, Urdu or Arabic. Typing /hijri does the same.
Pick a date on a calendar and a format,: Pick a date on a calendar and a format, Gregorian or Hijri, with month names in English, Urdu or Arabic. Alt+Shift+D inserts the date and Alt+Shift+T the time in the format you used last.
Alt+Shift+D and /today insert “{date}”. Alt+Shift+T and /time insert “{time}”.
Enter to insert · Esc to close: Enter to insert · Esc to close
Use Insert → Date & time instead. The da: Use Insert → Date & time instead. The date tools are not loaded in this window.
Select the whole document: the Markdown: Select the whole document: the Markdown in Simple mode, the page in Word, Inline and Read mode. Ribbon and outline are left out.
Open or create a document first, then se: Open or create a document first, then select its text.
Press Esc to go back to editing, then pa: Press Esc to go back to editing, then paste. Read mode does not change the document.
Paste the words on the clipboard without: Paste the words on the clipboard without their fonts, colors, links or tables. Also Ctrl+Alt+V.
Copy some text first, then paste it as p: Copy some text first, then paste it as plain text. The clipboard has no text right now.
Typing ( [ { or a quote adds the closing: Typing ( [ { or a quote adds the closing one and puts the cursor between. Typing the closing one steps over it, a selection gets wrapped, and Backspace removes an empty pair.
In Simple and Inline mode, * _ ` and ~~: In Simple and Inline mode, * _ ` and ~~ close themselves as well: type ** for **bold**. A * at the start of a line stays a bullet.
Typing $ adds the closing $ for an equat: Typing $ adds the closing $ for an equation. A number right after it ($5) keeps the dollar sign as typed.
Type /today, /time, /hijri or /date and: Type /today, /time, /hijri or /date and press Space or Enter. A small list shows the choices; Esc closes it.
Put the cursor in a word or select some: Put the cursor in a word or select some text first, then press Ctrl+D to select the next match.
Type to change every selected match at o: Type to change every selected match at once, or press Esc for one cursor. All matches are selected.
Select other text to look for, or press: Select other text to look for, or press Esc. There is no other match.
Put the cursor in a word or select some: Put the cursor in a word or select some text first, then press Alt+F3 to select every match.
Select other text to look for, or press: Select other text to look for, or press Esc. This is the only match.
Open a Markdown document first. Multiple: Open a Markdown document first. Multiple cursors work in Simple mode.
Switch to Simple mode (Ctrl+3) to use {f: Switch to Simple mode (Ctrl+3) to use {feature}. Word and Inline mode have one cursor; Simple mode edits the Markdown with as many as you like.
Simple mode: select the word at the curs: Simple mode: select the word at the cursor, then each next match with one more cursor. Type to change them all at once. Esc goes back to one cursor.
Simple mode: put a cursor on every match: Simple mode: put a cursor on every match of the selected text (or the word at the cursor). With several cursors on, Ctrl+Shift+L does the same.
Simple mode: add a cursor on the line ab: Simple mode: add a cursor on the line above, at the same column. Alt+click adds one anywhere.
Simple mode: add a cursor on the line be: Simple mode: add a cursor on the line below, at the same column. Alt+click adds one anywhere.
Remove the extra cursors and keep the la: Remove the extra cursors and keep the last one.
There is only one cursor now. Ctrl+D, Ct: There is only one cursor now. Ctrl+D, Ctrl+Alt+Up or Down, or Alt+click add more in Simple mode.

@notes.English (US): Language name (spelling and grammar of US English). Write it in the interface language.
@notes.English (UK): Language name (spelling and grammar of British English). Write it in the interface language.
@notes.Urdu: Language name, written in the interface language. The native name (اردو) is shown next to it separately.
@notes.Punjabi (Shahmukhi): Language name: Punjabi written in the Perso-Arabic (Shahmukhi) script.
@notes.English: Language name (also the name of the English keyboard).
@notes.{language} — {native}: Menu item: the language name in the interface language, then its own native name (for example "Urdu — اردو"). Keep both placeholders.
@notes.Urdu (اردو): Choice of month and day names in Insert → Date & time. Keep the native name in brackets.
@notes.Arabic (العربية): Choice of month and day names in Insert → Date & time. Keep the native name in brackets.
@notes.Urdu and Punjabi (Shahmukhi): Fills {language} in "Used for {language} text on the page…" (Options → Language → fonts).
@notes.Direction: Ribbon group name on Home (paragraph text direction). Short, about 12 characters.
@notes.Left to right: Menu item and status: text direction. Also used for a language pack’s writing direction.
@notes.Right to left: Menu item and status: text direction. Also used for a language pack’s writing direction.
@notes.From the language: Menu item: the page direction follows the document language.
@notes.Language: File → Options section name, and the ribbon label of the proofing language list (Review → Writing).
@notes.Version {version}: Version number of a language pack, for example "Version 2.1.0".
@notes.Font: {font}: The font a language pack uses, for example "Font: Noto Nastaliq Urdu".
@notes.system@@font: Fills {font} in "Font: {font}" when a language pack uses the computer’s own font.
@notes.{size} MB: File size in megabytes; use your language’s unit symbol.
@notes.{size} KB: File size in kilobytes; use your language’s unit symbol.
@notes.{count} words: Number of words in a language pack’s word list.
@notes.{count} checked so far: Number of words native speakers have checked in a language pack’s word list.
@notes.Help improve: Link next to a language pack: opens the guide for volunteers. Short.
@notes.Credits:: Label before the list of sources of a language pack’s word list.
@notes.Remove: Button: delete a language pack. In the Writing Assistant card: the suggestion is to delete the underlined words. Short button.
@notes.Download: Button: download and install a language pack. Short.
@notes.Update: Button (a verb): install the newer version of a language pack. Short.
@notes.Installed: Tag next to a language pack that is already installed. Short.
@notes.Built in: Tag next to English (US) and English (UK): they come with Markooj. Short.
@notes.{font} (default): A font in a list, marked as the one Markooj uses unless you choose another.
@notes.{reason} Installed languages keep workin: {reason} is a message from the language pack server, already in your language when Markooj has it.
@notes.{reason} You can also install a pack fro: {reason} is what to do first, for example "Check your internet connection, then click Try again."
@notes.Proofing language: {language}: Message after choosing the default proofing language.
Message after choosing the proofing language of the document (Review → Writing).
@notes.Markooj language pack: File type name in the Open dialog (.zip files).
@notes.Keyboard: Ribbon group and button on View, menu heading and Options heading: the typing keyboard (layout).
@notes.Standard: Short hint next to "Persian — فارسی" in the keyboard menu: the standard Persian layout. Short.
@notes.Phonetic: Short hint in the keyboard menu: a phonetic keyboard layout. Short.
@notes.Phonetic (CRULP): Short hint in the keyboard menu: the Urdu Phonetic layout by CRULP. Keep "CRULP".
@notes.Arabic 101: Short hint in the keyboard menu: the Windows Arabic (101) layout. Keep "101".
@notes.On-screen: Ribbon button (View → Keyboard): shows the on-screen keyboard. Short, about 10 characters.
@notes.Space: Key on the on-screen keyboard (the space bar).
@notes.Half space: Key on the on-screen keyboard: the zero-width non-joiner used in Persian and Urdu. Short.
@notes.Joiner: Name of the invisible zero-width joiner character, shown on a key. Short.
@notes.Switch keyboard: Ribbon button and ScreenTip title: English ⇄ the last right-to-left keyboard.
@notes.Keyboard: {layout}: ScreenTip of the keyboard chip on the status bar; {layout} is a layout name such as "Urdu Phonetic (CRULP)".
@notes.Switch to {language}: Keyboard menu item; {language} is Urdu, Arabic, Persian or Punjabi (Shahmukhi).
@notes.zabar (fatha): Name of a vowel mark, read by screen readers on the on-screen keyboard. Keep the Arabic term in brackets.
@notes.Aarab: Ribbon group on Home and Options heading: the vowel marks (harakat) of Urdu and Arabic writing. Use the word your readers use.
@notes.Zabar: Ribbon button: the vowel mark zabar (fatha). Short.
@notes.Zer: Ribbon button: the vowel mark zer (kasra). Short.
@notes.Pesh: Ribbon button: the vowel mark pesh (damma). Short.
@notes.Shadd: Ribbon button: the doubling mark shadd (shadda). Short.
@notes.Jazm: Ribbon button: the mark jazm (sukun). Short.
@notes.Remove Aarab: Big ribbon button (Home → Aarab), Word-style capitals. About 14 characters.
@notes.Hide Aarab: Ribbon button (Home → Aarab), Word-style capitals. Short.
@notes.From Word List: Ribbon button (Home → Aarab): add aarab from the language pack’s word list. Short.
@notes.Automatic: Choice in Options → Language → Aarab: show the group when it helps.
@notes.Su@@sunday short: Calendar column head for Sunday, at most 2 or 3 characters.
@notes.Mo@@monday short: Calendar column head for Monday, at most 2 or 3 characters.
@notes.Tu@@tuesday short: Calendar column head for Tuesday, at most 2 or 3 characters.
@notes.We@@wednesday short: Calendar column head for Wednesday, at most 2 or 3 characters.
@notes.Th@@thursday short: Calendar column head for Thursday, at most 2 or 3 characters.
@notes.Fr@@friday short: Calendar column head for Friday, at most 2 or 3 characters.
@notes.Sa@@saturday short: Calendar column head for Saturday, at most 2 or 3 characters.
@notes.Muharram: Hijri month name, shown under the calendar of Insert → Date & time.
@notes.Insert@@verb: Button that puts what the dialog prepared into the document: a date, table, link, equation, citation or cross-reference.
@notes.{day} {month} {year} AH: Hijri date under the calendar, for example "1 Ramadan 1447 AH". Order the parts as your language does; AH is the Hijri era.
@notes.dd/mm/yyyy: Name of a date format: day/month/year with two-digit day and month. Write the letters your language uses for day, month and year.
@notes.dd/mm/yy: Name of a date format with a two-digit year.
@notes.mm/dd/yyyy (US): Name of the US date format (month first).
@notes.yyyy-mm-dd (ISO): Name of the ISO date format. Keep "ISO".
@notes.yyyymmdd: Name of the compact date format (20261127).
@notes.yyyy year · MM month (MMMM name) · dd da: Help under the custom pattern box. Keep the pattern letters (yyyy, MM, MMMM, dd, dddd, HH, h, mm, a) exactly: they are codes. Translate only the words.
@notes.Gregorian: Calendar choice (the Western calendar). Short segment button.
@notes.Hijri: Calendar choice (the Islamic lunar calendar). Short segment button.
@notes.Today: Button under the calendar: go to today. Short.
@notes.Format: Screen reader name of the list of date formats.
@notes.Change…: Button in File → Options → Typing: opens the date format dialog.
@notes.Slash commands: Typing /today, /time, /date or /hijri in a document; also a switch in Options. The commands themselves stay /today etc.
@notes.Enter to insert · Esc to close: Footer of the slash-command list. Keep the key names Enter and Esc.
@notes.multiple cursors: Fills {feature} in "Switch to Simple mode (Ctrl+3) to use {feature}. …" (lower case in English).
@notes.Switch to Simple mode (Ctrl+3) to use {f: {feature} is a command name such as "Select next match" or "multiple cursors".
@notes.General: Writing goal: audience or domain “general” (for anyone, most writing).
@notes.Domain: Writing goal: the kind of writing (general, academic or business).
@notes.Correctness: Category of writing suggestions (spelling and grammar).
@notes.Delivery: Category of writing suggestions: tone for your goals.
@notes.correctness: Legend of underline colors in the Writing Assistant pane (lower case in English).
@notes.clarity: Legend of underline colors in the Writing Assistant pane (lower case in English).
@notes.engagement: Legend of underline colors in the Writing Assistant pane (lower case in English).
@notes.delivery: Legend of underline colors in the Writing Assistant pane (lower case in English).
@notes.Underlines:: Start of the color legend at the bottom of the Writing Assistant pane.
@notes.All: Tab in the Writing Assistant: all categories of suggestions. Very short.
@notes.remove: Suggestion in the Writing Assistant list: delete the underlined words (lower case after an arrow).
@notes.(remove): Suggestion chip in Spelling and Grammar (F7): delete the underlined words.
@notes.Goals: {audience} · {formality} · {domai: Button in the Writing Assistant pane showing the three writing goals, for example "Goals: General · Neutral · General".
@notes.Goals: Ribbon button and ScreenTip: writing goals (audience, formality, domain).
@notes.noun: Part of speech heading in the Thesaurus (lower case in English).
@notes.verb: Part of speech heading in the Thesaurus (lower case in English).
@notes.adjective: Part of speech heading in the Thesaurus (lower case in English).
@notes.adverb: Part of speech heading in the Thesaurus (lower case in English).
@notes.Antonyms:: Label before words of opposite meaning in the Thesaurus.
@notes.{index} of {total}: Position in Spelling and Grammar (F7), for example "3 of 12".
@notes.Change to: Label of the box with the replacement text in Spelling and Grammar (F7).
@notes.Change: Button in Spelling and Grammar (F7): replace the word, like Word. Short.
@notes.Ignore: Button in Spelling and Grammar (F7): skip this one. Short.
@notes.Ignore All: Button in Spelling and Grammar (F7), like Word: skip this word everywhere. Short.
@notes.Ignore Rule: Button in Spelling and Grammar (F7): turn off this grammar rule. Short.
@notes.Add to Dictionary: Button in Spelling and Grammar (F7), like Word. Short.
@notes.Accept: ScreenTip title of a suggested fix in the Writing Assistant card.
@notes.Dismiss: Button in the Writing Assistant card and menu: hide this suggestion.
@notes.Why?: Button that opens the explanation of a writing rule. Very short.
@notes.Wrong: Screen reader name of the ✕ before a wrong example.
@notes.Right@@correct: Screen reader name of the ✓ before a right (correct) example. Not the direction.
@notes.Harper grammar checker: Credit under a grammar explanation. Keep the name Harper.
@notes.Checking off: Status-bar text when spelling and writing checks are both off. Short.
@notes.{category}: {n}: Tooltip on the status bar: a category of suggestions and how many, for example "Clarity: 3".
@notes.My dictionary ({n})…: Button in Options → Writing; {n} is the number of words in your dictionary.
@notes.Turn ignored rules back on ({n}): Button in Options → Writing; {n} is the number of rules turned off.
@notes.Proofing: Ribbon group on Review (spelling, thesaurus, word count), as in Word.
@notes.Writing: Ribbon group on Review and File → Options section: the Writing Assistant.
@notes.Spelling & Grammar: Big ribbon button on Review, as in Word.
@notes.Technical terms: Ribbon button on Review: accept technical terms and place names. Short.
@notes.Suggest words: Ribbon button on Review: word completion while typing. Short.
@notes.Suggestion: Heading of the right-click menu over an underlined word when its rule has no title.
@notes.Pseudo (testing): Name of the test language that developers and translators use to find text that is not translated yet. Shown only to them.
